summary: Cass County steel lookout tower about five miles east of Douglassville, described in a 1958 Coast and Geodetic Survey record with a glass cab and about 100 ft height; the FFLA lists it as gone.

facts.design: Glass-enclosed cab on a four-legged steel structure, per a 1958 survey station description
facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone; no source read describes the site today

corrections.why: The town and the NGS station record on Central US Lookouts spell it Douglassville; the FFLA list uses one s. Editor to decide whether the display name changes.

notes_for_editor: Height_m 30.5 is the converted 'about 100 feet' from the NGS record, not a measured figure. The NGS record gives 1958 directions from the Douglassville post office to the station; they were left out because they describe a route to a site now listed as gone. Texas Escapes says most of the town's 20th-century history is unavailable, so no town-side history is added. Record coordinates were not checked against a fetched town coordinate. Story is about 115 words. Next leads: Cavallerano, Fire in the Piney Woods (2025), and Texas Forest Service archives, for build and removal dates.
